ipc.expression: sendToMain(ToMain.GPU_HEALTH, { issue, platform: process.platform, vendorName, vaDriverMissing, packages })

comments.text: // GPU device selection and runtime GPU health checks
// Universal PCI vendor ids
// Linux: /dev/dri/renderD* -> name via sysfs PCI vendor/device ids
// a single render node offers no real choice — "Auto" is already correct; hide the selector
// macOS: only a power PREFERENCE exists (see the header). Offered only on actual dual-GPU machines.
// labels are i18n'd in the frontend (settings.gpu_high_performance)
// Windows: no reliable persistable mechanism (see header) — selector not shown
// ---- application (BEFORE app ready; switches must precede GPU process launch) ----
// no GPU process to pin
// env override kept as a no-rebuild debugging lever; the Settings value is the product mechanism
// device gone (eGPU unplugged, hardware change): fall back to auto instead of a dead GPU process
// Windows: nothing to apply (see header)
// ---- runtime health check -> verbose user notification ----
// hardware video decode needs a *_drv_video.so VA driver; many installs (e.g. Ubuntu live ISOs) ship none
// "enabled..." / "hardware..." = hardware acceleration active
// Resolves once Chromium GPU feature status has settled
// Probes whether video hardware-decodes in the active renderer
// whether an installed VA driver actually serves this vendor's GPU (Ubuntu ships several
// foreign-vendor Gallium drivers by default)
// PCI vendor name of a DRM render node via sysfs (same source as listLinuxRenderNodes)
// vendors of every GPU with a render node (decode can come from any of them, not just the active one)
// probe verdict wins; when it couldn't run, fall back to the (optimistic) feature status
// active GPU vendor (for the VA package suggestion + naming the device in the message)
// compositing dead = GPU init failed entirely; otherwise compositing is fine but video decode is
// software (a few CPU cores per 4K60 stream — choppy playback, starved outputs)
// driver scan feeds the remediation message only: target the GPU selected in Settings, or on
// auto every GPU missing its vendor driver (on dual-GPU machines the fix is often the iGPU's)
